text: The contractual notice is a rwb-comms element: rwb-partner requests it on the P6 contract with the partner, the case, the notice type and its template, receives the notice reference and holds it in its decision record and its answer, and writes no notice row, no template and no dispatch status itself.
why: The ownership rows give S9 three tables, none of them a notice; TSD S9 T3.1 defines partner, partner_instruction and partner_user only; FSD S9 T5.2 sends notices to P6 and the event catalogue gives NoticeGenerated and NoticeDispatched to Communications. The legacy Data table lists the notice row (DF-LEG-015 to DF-LEG-023) so the notice exists as a record and cannot be dropped, and a notice table declared in S9 would give the service a fourth table and a migration no document owns.
read: Context pack ownership rows (3 tables, 6 REST operations, EV-20 and EV-21, no job); TSD S9 T2, T3.1, T5.2 and T5.3; FSD S9 T5.2 and A2.11.2; Event and Messaging Design v4 events EV-13 and EV-14; legacy RWB-E7-014 Data and Endpoints; Template and Rules v1 R9
confirm: Solution architect and the rwb-comms owner, before wave 4 starts
impact: The notice stays one record in one service, this service holds only its reference, and a build that creates a notice table or a notice path fails the review

text: No partner route set exists, so the decision record of the notice carries the rule ID and the version in force as the workspace supplies them and no rule row, no package and no rule ID set is declared; the nearest rows of the Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 are R-UNI-25 to R-UNI-29, which recall work and do not issue a notice, and the rule ID, its version and the rule that decides a missed target carry the placeholder until a partner route set is published.
why: The legacy criterion requires that the result be written to the decision log with the rule version, DP-03 requires the rule ID and the version, and the Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 has no R-PRM rows at all: the nine route sets it holds are restructure, guarantee, litigation, asset disposal, debt sale, write-off, deviation, universal and deed in lieu. Citing R-UNI-25 to R-UNI-29 as the notice's rule would misattribute a recall to a notice, and inventing a rule ID would create a row no business owner approved.

confirm: Business lead and the rule owner in rwb-decision, before wave 4 starts
impact: The record is written with the value in force and the placeholder, no rule row or package is added to the service, and the rule arrives as a package row without a code change

text: The cure period starts at the notice's sent date and its length is reference data read with its version; the length, the parameter name and the value are Not specified in the source documents, and the expiry is tracked by the case stage's timer in P3, so this service holds no timer row, starts no Schedule and writes no cure-period column.
why: The FSD names the cure period as an effect of the notice (A2.11.1, A2.11.2) and gives it no length, no list and no parameter; cure_period_days in R-RES-27 to R-RES-29 belongs to a broken treatment plan and not to a partner; and the ownership rows give this service no job and no timer table. Writing a length in code would break BR-S9-011, and a timer declared here would take the case clock from rwb-case.

text: The notice is submitted on API-S9-002 POST /cases/{caseId}/instructions, the operation the legacy endpoint table of RWB-E7-014 names, with the Idempotency-Key header; the contract declares no notice path, no notice property and no notice type value, so the request property that would carry the notice facts carries the placeholder, and partner_user is owned with no property declared because TSD S9 T3.1 gives it no field.
why: The legacy story sends the notice and its endpoint table gives the instruction operations and no notice operation; TSD S9 T-A.1 and T-A.2 publish six operations and none of them is a notice, and the ownership rows give six operations only. A notice path invented for this feature would add an operation no owner published, and a property invented for the notice would add a business value no source holds. partner_user appears in the ownership rows and in no field catalogue, so a property of it would be invented.

text: The notice moves the partner from ACTIVE to ON_NOTICE over LOV-PANEL; the two exits from ON_NOTICE, back to ACTIVE when the cure is met and to SUSPENDED when it lapses, have no trigger, no rule row and no owning story in any source and are not built here; and the refusal of a partner at SUSPENDED or EXITED, with an ended contract or already at ON_NOTICE, is a 409 whose message carries the placeholder.
why: LOV-PANEL already carries ON_NOTICE (TSD S9 T3.2) and the legacy feature's effect is a notice on a missed target, so the panel status is the one field this service can change; but no source states that the notice sets the status, no rule row names either exit, and no message exists for the refusal. Leaving the exits unbuilt and the message unspecified keeps the story inside its own deliverable and adds no invented business value.

text: The target a partner's score is measured against is versioned reference data read from the owner the R3 default ruling names (rwb-case) at its version in force, on one hop with a 2 s budget and a fake; the threshold, the measure, the parameter name and the value are Not specified in the source documents, DP-06 and DP-07 are absent from the pattern set of the key, and the plan's C row is empty while the row is consumed.

Writing a threshold in code would break BR-S9-011 and the legacy guardrail, and declaring the read as the published reference-data contract would take a dependency row the plan does not hold.
